$comment: One photograph for each of the app's own playlist folders on the phones: the folder of the moods, the
folder of the decades, and one folder per mood. Each is shown behind the folder frame, washed in the
folder's colour, with the folder's name in the frame's bottom bar.
THEY ARE NOT THE LISTS' PHOTOGRAPHS. A folder holds lists that wear the photographs in
playlist-photos.json, so a folder shows a picture of its own and reads as a folder and not as one more
list. None of these ids is in playlist-photos.json.
The rules of playlist-photos.json apply here too: the ids are pinned and fetched without a key when
a source is pinned; every one is under the Pexels License; no person is in any of them, each was
looked at before it was kept; they are cut to a centred square at `edge` pixels.
'folder' is the key the apps look a folder up by: 'moods', 'decades', or 'mood:' and the mood's kind
as the computer spells it. 'name' is the folder's English name for the credit line on the About screen.
Run: python scripts/gen_folder_photos.py. It writes the files and the tables into the iPhone and
Android apps; gen_credits.py credits the photographers.
